advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider auto-applying/enforcing `requires_posix_named_semaphore` for tests using multiprocessing primitives (or note the marker is a manual convention) so the doc's 'exactly the tests' invariant cannot silently drift.
evidence: docs/local-dev-env.md: 'exactly the tests whose contract is process-level multiprocessing behavior are skipped'

search shows the marker applied only at test_atomic_completion_close.py:395, test_doctor_locks.py:150, test_marker_fcntl_guard.py:80, test_network_guard_local_ipc.py:71 — with no collection-time guard tying it to multiprocessing usage
advisory.finding: The `requires_posix_named_semaphore` marker is applied by hand to exactly four tests with no automated enforcement that multiprocessing-based tests carry it, but docs/local-dev-env.md asserts 'exactly the tests whose contract is process-level multiprocessing behavior are skipped' as an invariant. A future test that constructs multiprocessing synchronization primitives without the marker will hard-fail (not loud-skip) under the sandbox, silently violating the documented guarantee.
scenarios: A new test constructs mp.Event()/mp.Process() without adding the marker; it fails under a semaphore-denied sandbox instead of being counted-skipped.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives the real tests/conftest.py pytest_runtest_setup hook (e.g. via pytester loading the repo conftest with a monkeypatched/injected denied probe) rather than reimplementing the hook body inline.
evidence: tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_0eba.py:64 defines its own `def pytest_runtest_setup(item):` in makeconftest with a hand-written body rather than importing the real hook
Production hook under review: tests/conftest.py:215 `def pytest_runtest_setup(item: pytest.Item) -> None:` calling `posix_named_semaphore_probe()` (conftest.py:219)

search of tests/ for `pytest_runtest_setup` shows the real one only in tests/conftest.py:215; the 0eba test file only defines parallel copies at lines 64 and 120 — the real hook has no test that drives it

Regression-blindness (criterion d): renaming the marker, breaking the probe wiring, or reordering record_counted_skip/pytest.skip in tests/conftest.py would not fail these tests because they run their own copy of the logic
advisory.finding: The two pytester integration tests reimplement the production pytest_runtest_setup hook inline in makeconftest instead of driving the real hook in tests/conftest.py; the real hook (marker-name gating, posix_named_semaphore_probe() call, reason-fallback branch, record_counted_skip+pytest.skip sequence) is never exercised, so a regression in the real conftest hook would leave these tests green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Cover the empty-reason fallback branch of the conftest hook with a CapabilityProbe(False, "") input asserting the default reason is used and counted.
evidence: tests/conftest.py:222 `reason = probe.reason or "POSIX named semaphore unavailable"`
Named violating input: a CapabilityProbe(False, "") (available False, empty reason) reaching the hook would take the fallback branch, but no test constructs a denied probe with an empty reason
test_posix_named_semaphore_probe_reports_unavailable_on_eperm asserts a non-empty reason (tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_0eba.py:22-23); pytester tests hardcode a non-empty reason (line 68-70)
advisory.finding: The `reason = probe.reason or "POSIX named semaphore unavailable"` fallback branch in the real hook (when a denied probe returns an empty reason) is not covered by any test — the unit tests always supply a non-empty reason and the pytester tests hardcode a reason string.
